functions.signature:
-- server
vehicle createVehicle ( number model, number x, number y, number z
                        [, number rx = 0, number ry = 0, number rz = 0,
                           number col1, number col2, number col3, number col4 ] )

-- client

                        [, number x, number y, number z,
                           number rx = 0, number ry = 0, number rz ] )

variants.text: vehicle createVehicle ( number model, number x, number y, number z [, number rx = 0, number ry = 0, number rz = 0, number col1, number col2, number col3, number col4 ] )

functions.returns: the new vehicle, or `nil` if the model is outside the `400`–`611` range. On the client it also returns `nil` when creation fails, and the reason is written to the debug console.

params.name: model
params.description: Model ID, between `400` and `611`.

params.name: x, y, z
params.description: Spawn position. Required on the server, optional on the client.

params.name: rx, ry
params.description: Spawn rotation, in degrees.

params.name: rz
params.description: Spawn rotation around the vertical axis, in degrees.

params.name: col1 … col4
params.description: **Server only.** Palette colour indices, `0` to `127`. Values outside that range are clamped into it.

functions.description: Creates a vehicle in the world.
examples:
local vehicle = createVehicle(411, x, y, z)
setElementRotation(vehicle, rx, ry, rz)

-- server
local car = createVehicle(411, 1959.55, -1714.46, 15.5)
setElementData(car, "owner", "nobody")

-- client: a showroom car, on this screen only
local showroom = createVehicle(411)

functions.description: Fires an event on the server.
examples:
-- the server's answer
addEvent("onPurchaseResult", true)
addEventHandler("onPurchaseResult", root, function(approved, reason)
    if approved then
        outputDebugString("purchase complete")
    else
        outputDebugString("purchase refused: " .. reason, 2)
    end
end)

bindKey("f2", "down", function()
    -- just the item name; the price is the server's business
    triggerServerEvent("onPlayerBuy", localPlayer, "armour")
end)

local prices = { armour = 500, helmet = 150 }

addEvent("onPlayerBuy", true)   -- the `true` is what lets the client fire it
addEventHandler("onPlayerBuy", root, function(item)
    local player = client        -- who actually sent the packet
    local price = prices[item]   -- price from the server's table, not the client's

    if not price then
        triggerClientEvent(player, "onPurchaseResult", player, false, "no such item")
        return
    end

    local balance = getElementData(player, "money") or 0
    if balance < price then
        triggerClientEvent(player, "onPurchaseResult", player, false, "not enough money")
        return
    end

    setElementData(player, "money", balance - price)
    triggerClientEvent(player, "onPurchaseResult", player, true)
end)

functions.description:
Performs an HTTP request and hands the response to a callback.

There are two ways to call it. The modern one, with an options table:
examples: bool fetchRemote ( string url [, string queueName, number attempts = 10, number timeout = 10000 ], function callback [, string postData, bool postIsBinary = false, ... ] )

-- GET: reading a JSON response
fetchRemote("https://api.example.com/status", {}, function(body, info)
    if not info.success then
        outputDebugString("API request failed: " .. info.statusCode, 1)
        return
    end

    local data = fromJSON(body)
    if type(data) ~= "table" then
        outputDebugString("the API answered with something that is not JSON", 2)
        return
    end

    outputDebugString("players on the site: " .. tostring(data.online))
end)

functions.description: Creates a texture you draw into yourself.
examples:
local sign = dxCreateRenderTarget(256, 128, true)
local needsRedraw = true

addEventHandler("onClientRender", root, function()
    if not sign then return end

    -- 1. draw into the target, only when the contents changed
    if needsRedraw then
        dxSetRenderTarget(sign, true)
        dxDrawRectangle(0, 0, 256, 128, tocolor(0, 0, 0, 200))
        dxDrawText("MTAX", 0, 0, 256, 128, tocolor(255, 255, 255, 255), 3, "default-bold", "center", "center")
        dxSetRenderTarget()          -- back to drawing on the screen
        needsRedraw = false
    end

    -- 2. use the target like any other image
    dxDrawImage(60, 60, 256, 128, sign)
end)

addEventHandler("onClientResourceStop", resourceRoot, function()
    -- 3. free it once you are done
    if sign then destroyElement(sign) end
end)

params.description: How long to wait for the result, in milliseconds. `0` checks once and returns straight away. A positive number waits up to that many milliseconds. A negative number, `-1` by convention, waits for as long as the query takes.

end

functions.name: setPedAnimation
functions.signature:
bool setPedAnimation ( ped thePed [, string block, string anim, number time = -1, bool loop = true,
                       bool updatePosition = true, bool interruptable = true, bool freezeLastFrame = true,
                       number blendTime = 250, bool restoreTaskOnAnimEnd = false ] )

variants.text: bool setPedAnimation ( ped thePed [, string block, string anim, number time = -1, bool loop = true, bool updatePosition = true, bool interruptable = true, bool freezeLastFrame = true, number blendTime = 250, bool restoreTaskOnAnimEnd = false ] )

functions.returns: `true` if at least one ped got the animation. Passing `true` for `block` or `anim` returns `false`.

params.name: thePed
params.description: Ped, or a parent element.

params.name: block
params.description: Animation block. `nil` or `false` stops the current animation.

params.name: anim
params.description: Animation name inside the block. `nil` or `false` stops the current one.

params.name: time
params.description: Duration in milliseconds. `-1` lets the animation run to its natural end.

params.name: loop
params.description: Restarts the animation when it finishes.

params.name: updatePosition
params.description: Lets the animation move the ped through the world.

params.name: interruptable
params.description: Allows a player action to cut the animation short.

params.name: freezeLastFrame
params.description: Leaves the ped frozen on the last frame when the animation ends.

params.name: blendTime
params.description: Blend from the current pose into the animation, in milliseconds.

params.name: restoreTaskOnAnimEnd
params.description: Accepted for compatibility; currently has no effect.

functions.description: Plays an animation on the ped, or stops the one that is running.
examples:
-- dance
setPedAnimation(player, "DANCING", "dnce_M_a", -1, true)

-- stop
setPedAnimation(player)

functions.description: Creates a blip that stays at a fixed position.
examples:
-- server: a yellow meeting point, visible from far away
local point = createBlip(1481.0, -1770.0, 18.8, 0, 3, 255, 220, 0, 255, 0, 500)

-- server: a blip only the player on the mission can see
addEventHandler("onPlayerJoin", root, function()
    createBlip(2495.0, -1670.0, 13.5, 41, 2, 0, 200, 255, 255, 0, 16383, source)
end)

-- client: the same meeting point, on this screen only
local point = createBlip(1481.0, -1770.0, 18.8, 0, 3, 255, 220, 0, 255, 0, 500)

functions.description: Creates a point light at a world position.
examples:
-- a blue light flashing above the player
local x, y, z = getElementPosition(localPlayer)
local beacon = createLight(0, x, y, z + 1.5, 8, 0, 80, 255)

setTimer(function()
    if not isElement(beacon) then return end
    local r = getLightColor(beacon)
    if r == 0 then
        setLightColor(beacon, 255, 0, 0)
    else
        setLightColor(beacon, 0, 80, 255)
    end
end, 400, 0)

functions.signature: bool passwordVerify ( string hash, string password )

variants.text: bool passwordVerify ( string hash, string password )

functions.returns: `true` if the password matches. `false` if it does not, or if the hash is malformed.

params.name: hash
params.description: The stored hash, exactly as `passwordHash` returned it.

params.name: password
params.description: The password the player typed.

functions.description: Checks a password against a hash.
examples:
local accounts = {}

addCommandHandler("register", function(source, cmd, password)
    if source == false or not password then return end

    local name = getPlayerName(source)
    if accounts[name] then
        outputDebugString("an account for " .. name .. " already exists", 2)
        return
    end

    local hash = passwordHash(password)
    if not hash then
        outputDebugString("could not create an account for " .. name, 1)
        return
    end

    accounts[name] = hash          -- store the hash, never the password
    setElementData(source, "loggedIn", true)
end)

addCommandHandler("login", function(source, cmd, password)
    if source == false or not password then return end

    local name = getPlayerName(source)
    local hash = accounts[name]

    -- same answer for an unknown account and a wrong password, so nobody
    -- can work out which accounts exist by guessing
    if not hash or not passwordVerify(hash, password) then
        outputDebugString("login refused for " .. name, 2)
        return
    end

    setElementData(source, "loggedIn", true)
end)

functions.description: Casts a line between two points and describes the first thing it hits.
examples:
-- what is the camera pointing at?
addCommandHandler("aim", function()
    local cx, cy, cz, lx, ly, lz = getCameraMatrix()
    local dx, dy, dz = lx - cx, ly - cy, lz - cz
    local hit, x, y, z, element = processLineOfSight(
        cx, cy, cz,
        cx + dx * 100, cy + dy * 100, cz + dz * 100)

    if not hit then
        outputDebugString("nothing in the way")
    elseif element then
        outputDebugString("hit a " .. getElementType(element))
    else
        outputDebugString("hit scenery at " .. x .. ", " .. y .. ", " .. z)
    end
end)

events.name: onClientPedsProcessed
events.description:
Fired once per frame, after every character in the world has been updated and before anything is drawn.

**Source** — the root element (`root`).

This event has no parameters.

**Cancellable** — no.

This is the earliest hook of the frame. Use it to read the state of the world before deciding what to draw — who is nearby, who is aiming at whom, who just moved. Drawing works here too, but anything you draw sits underneath whatever the other three hooks draw.

pt.description:
Disparado uma vez por quadro, depois que todos os personagens do mundo foram atualizados e antes de qualquer coisa ser desenhada.

**Source** — a raiz (`root`).

Este evento não tem parâmetros.

**Cancelável** — não.

É o gancho mais cedo do quadro. Serve para ler o estado do mundo antes de decidir o que desenhar — quem está por perto, quem está mirando em quem, quem acabou de se mexer. Desenhar aqui também funciona, mas o que sair daqui fica embaixo de tudo que os outros três ganchos desenharem.

Fired once per frame, immediately before [`onClientRender`](#onclientrender).

params.description: Milliseconds elapsed since the previous `onClientPreRender`. It arrives as `0` on the very first frame.

events.name: onClientRender
events.description:
Fired once per frame, in the middle of the drawing trio.

**Source** — the root element (`root`).

This event has no parameters.

**Cancellable** — no.

This is the hook **nearly everything drawn on screen** hangs off. Because a draw only lasts a frame, a HUD is literally "redraw the same thing 60 times a second". What you want to keep out of that loop is everything that does not change per frame: the screen size, the colours, the fixed positions. Work those out once, outside the handler.

pt.description:
Disparado uma vez por quadro, no meio do trio de desenho.

**Source** — a raiz (`root`).

Este evento não tem parâmetros.

**Cancelável** — não.

Este é o gancho em que **quase todo o desenho na tela** se apoia. Como o desenho vale por um quadro só, uma HUD é literalmente "redesenhar a mesma coisa 60 vezes por segundo". O que sai da conta é tudo que não muda a cada quadro: o tamanho da tela, as cores, as posições fixas. Calcule isso uma vez, fora do manipulador.

events.name: onClientHUDRender
events.description:
Fired once per frame, after [`onClientRender`](#onclientrender). It is the last hook of the frame.

**Source** — the root element (`root`).

This event has no parameters.

**Cancellable** — no.

The only difference from `onClientRender` is draw order, and that is precisely what makes it useful: what you draw here sits **above** everything the other resources drew in `onClientRender`. It is the right place for an overlay that must never be covered — a death notice, a countdown, a full-screen tint.

pt.description:
Disparado uma vez por quadro, depois do [`onClientRender`](#onclientrender). É o último gancho do quadro.

**Source** — a raiz (`root`).

Este evento não tem parâmetros.

**Cancelável** — não.

A diferença para o `onClientRender` é só a ordem de desenho, e é exatamente por isso que ele é útil: o que você desenha aqui fica **por cima** de tudo que os outros resources desenharam no `onClientRender`. É o lugar certo para uma sobreposição que nunca pode ser tapada — um aviso de morte, uma contagem regressiva, uma vinheta de tela cheia.

events.name: onClientElementStreamIn
events.description:
Fired when an element created by the server comes into streaming range and starts existing in the player's world.

**Source** — the element that streamed in.

This event has no parameters.

**Cancellable** — no.

This is the right place to set up whatever depends on the element actually being in the world — applying a shader, starting a positional sound, kicking off an animation.

Adding a handler also triggers a catch-up pass: on the next processing pass, that new handler runs once for every already-streamed element inside its propagation scope. State is checked again just before the call; if an element streams out or is destroyed in the meantime, its replay is dropped.

pt.description:
Disparado quando um elemento criado pelo servidor entra na distância de streaming e passa a existir no mundo do jogador.

**Source** — o elemento que entrou.

Este evento não tem parâmetros.

**Cancelável** — não.

É o lugar certo para preparar o que depende do elemento estar realmente no mundo — aplicar um shader, ligar um som posicional, começar uma animação.

Ao adicionar um manipulador, o cliente também faz um *catch-up*: no processamento seguinte, esse novo manipulador é chamado uma vez para cada elemento já transmitido dentro do seu escopo de propagação. O estado é conferido novamente antes da chamada; se o elemento sair do streaming ou for destruído nesse intervalo, a repetição é descartada.

events.name: onClientElementStreamOut
events.description:
Fired when an element created by the server leaves streaming range and stops existing in the player's world.

**Source** — the element that streamed out.

This event has no parameters.

**Cancellable** — no.

The element is still valid after the event — it just is not materialised in the world any more. This is where you undo whatever you set up in [`onClientElementStreamIn`](#onclientelementstreamin).

pt.description:
Disparado quando um elemento criado pelo servidor sai da distância de streaming e deixa de existir no mundo do jogador.

**Source** — o elemento que saiu.

Este evento não tem parâmetros.

**Cancelável** — não.

O elemento continua válido depois do evento — ele só não está mais materializado no mundo. É aqui que você desfaz o que preparou no [`onClientElementStreamIn`](#onclientelementstreamin).

events.name: onClientElementDestroy
events.description:
Fired when an element is about to stop existing.

**Source** — the element that is about to go.

This event has no parameters.

**Cancellable** — no.

The element is still valid inside the handler: you can read its type, its position and its data one last time. It covers **every** element type, not only the ones created by the server. After the event, every handler attached directly to that element is removed automatically.
events.source: the element that is about to go.

pt.description:
Disparado quando um elemento está prestes a deixar de existir.

**Source** — o elemento que vai sumir.

Este evento não tem parâmetros.

**Cancelável** — não.

O elemento ainda é válido durante o manipulador: dá para ler o tipo, a posição, os dados dele uma última vez. Vale para **todos** os tipos de elemento, não só os criados pelo servidor. Depois do evento, qualquer manipulador preso diretamente ao elemento é removido automaticamente.

events.name: onPlayerConnect
events.description:
Fires when a client finishes connecting, **before** it joins the server. This is where you turn someone away: the player has not received any world data yet.

**Source** — the root element (`root`). The player's element is not part of the server yet at this point, so attach the handler to `root`.

params.description: Nickname the client asked for.
Address the client connected from.
Always empty — the password is never handed to the handler.
Sequential list of the identifiers available for this connection.
Network protocol number the server is running.
The same number written as `"0.major.minor"`.

pt.description:
Disparado quando um cliente termina de se conectar, **antes** de ele entrar no servidor. É o momento de barrar alguém: o jogador ainda não recebeu nenhum dado do mundo.

**Source** — a raiz (`root`). O elemento do jogador ainda não faz parte do servidor neste ponto, então prenda o manipulador em `root`.

params.description: Apelido que o cliente pediu.
Endereço de onde o cliente se conectou.
Sempre vazia — a senha nunca é entregue ao manipulador.
Lista sequencial dos identificadores disponíveis para esta conexão.
Número do protocolo de rede que o servidor está usando.
O mesmo número escrito como `"0.maior.menor"`.

pt.source: a raiz (root). O elemento do jogador ainda não faz parte do servidor neste ponto, então prenda o manipulador em root.

events.description:
Fires before any server command handler when a player is the source. This happens both for a line typed by the player in F8 — automatically forwarded by the client after local handlers and `onClientConsole` — and for [`executeCommandHandler`](https://wiki.mtax.com.br/en/scripting/functions/shared/command/#executecommandhandler) called on the server with that player. Comandos do console do servidor não disparam este evento.

events.name: onConsole
events.description:
Fires after a line passes through the server's Lua command system, with the command and its arguments. It fires even when no Lua handler picked the command up.

Lines typed into the server console that match built-ins — such as `start`, `stop`, `status`, `ac` or `shutdown` — are resolved before Lua and **do not** fire `onConsole`. This exception applies only to the server console: the same word received from F8 or run through `executeCommandHandler` still follows the Lua flow.

**Source** — the root element (`root`) for a line typed into the server console; the player for a line they typed in F8 or one run on their behalf through [`executeCommandHandler`](https://wiki.mtax.com.br/en/scripting/functions/shared/command/#executecommandhandler).

A exceção vale apenas para o console do servidor: a mesma palavra recebida do F8 ou executada por `executeCommandHandler` continua percorrendo o fluxo Lua.

**Source** — a raiz (`root`) para uma linha digitada no console do servidor; o jogador para uma linha digitada por ele no F8 ou executada em nome dele por [`executeCommandHandler`](https://wiki.mtax.com.br/pt/scripting/functions/shared/command/#executecommandhandler).

manifestKeys.name: resource_info
manifestKeys.description: Free-form text pairs read back by `getResourceInfo`.

manifestKeys.name: server_files
manifestKeys.description: `.lua` only. Runs on the server and is never sent to the client.

manifestKeys.name: client_files
manifestKeys.description: `.lua` only. Downloaded and executed on the client.

manifestKeys.name: files
manifestKeys.description: Assets downloaded by the client. Anything **except** `.lua`.

manifestKeys.name: map_files
manifestKeys.description: Map XML read by the server. Never `.lua`, never borrowed.

manifestKeys.name: ui_page
manifestKeys.description: HTML entry point of the resource UI. Must also appear in `files`.

manifestKeys.name: loadscreen
manifestKeys.description: Marks the resource as a loading screen, downloaded before every other.

manifestKeys.name: loadscreen_manual_shutdown
manifestKeys.description: Keeps the load screen up until `shutdownLoadingScreen` is called.

manifestKeys.name: exports
manifestKeys.description: Function names this resource offers to others through `exports`/`call`.

manifestKeys.name: escrow_files
manifestKeys.description: Files the portal build leaves **unprotected** on purpose (config a server owner has to edit). Read by the portal only — the runtime does not know the field exists. Each entry has to be a file the build would otherwise protect: a `.lua`, or a `dff`/`txd`/`col`/`ifp`, already declared in another list.

globals.name: root
globals.description: Root of the element tree. A handler attached here catches an event wherever it came from.

globals.name: resourceRoot
globals.description: This resource's own root element. Everything it creates hangs off it.

globals.name: source
globals.description: Inside an event handler: the element the event came from.

globals.name: client
globals.description: Inside a handler for a remote event: the player who triggered it. `nil` otherwise — always validate it.

globals.name: eventName
globals.description: Inside an event handler: the name of the running event.

globals.name: sourceResource
globals.description: The resource whose script called `triggerEvent`. `nil` when the engine fired it.

globals.name: sourceResourceRoot
globals.description: That resource's root element, `nil` in the same cases.

globals.name: exports
globals.description: Proxy table for calling another resource's exported functions: `exports.bank:getBalance(player)`.
